topStories.headline: Lower Haight Residents Win Secondary Review of Planned Ficus Removals on Waller Street
topStories.dek: A community campaign stopped the immediate emergency removal of seven mature ficus trees near Steiner Street, forcing a second look from city officials.
topStories.body:
More than 400 Lower Haight residents contacted local officials this month to protest planned emergency removals of seven mature ficus trees on Waller Street near Steiner, according to the Lower Haight Local, the neighborhood's volunteer-run nonprofit newspaper. In response, the office of District 5 Supervisor Bilal Mahmood secured a secondary review of the removals before any work could proceed.

The trees in question sit on a stretch of Waller Street that has been a flashpoint for urban-forestry disputes for years. SF Public Works has broad authority to remove ficus trees citywide under a 2014 director's order that lowered the removal standard for the species, citing risks from limb failure and root damage. Under that policy, trees determined to be vulnerable to failure are posted with 30-day public notices, and any resident may file a protest triggering a City Hall hearing.

The Lower Haight Local, a 501(c)(3) nonprofit that prints monthly and distributes free copies around the neighborhood, reported the story on its August 20 front page. The paper noted that the scale of resident response — more than 400 contacts — was unusually high and prompted the supervisor's office to intervene before the removal timeline moved forward.

The outcome of the secondary review has not yet been announced. Residents who want to track the case can monitor SF Public Works' monthly tree-removal hearing schedule at sfpublicworks.org.

topStories.headline: SF Planning Adopts Historic Survey Findings for Haight Street and Cole Valley Commercial Districts
topStories.dek: A formal preservation survey adopted in June documents the historical and architectural significance of commercial properties along Haight Street and Cole Valley, setting the stage for potential landmark designations.
topStories.body:
San Francisco's Historic Preservation Commission formally adopted Resolution R-1598 in June 2026, approving the SF Survey Findings for the Haight Street, Cole Valley, and Divisadero Street Neighborhood Commercial Districts. The resolution, stemming from a public hearing held June 3, is part of the city's ongoing Citywide Cultural Resources Survey — a multi-year Planning Department program to identify and document places of cultural, historical, and architectural significance.

For Haight-Ashbury and Cole Valley, the survey is focused on Haight Street from Central to Shrader, cataloguing buildings and sites within the commercial corridors. The findings build on a separate 2024 document — the Citywide Historic Context Statement for Counterculture (1965–1975) — which identified specific locations tied to the Summer of Love era but did not index them within the neighborhood's full geographic scope.

The Haight Ashbury Neighborhood Council (HANC), which covers the area from Arguello to Divisadero and Fulton to 17th Street, has been actively engaging residents to supplement the official survey. At its July 9 meeting, HANC President Richard Ivanhoe invited neighbors to help identify historic treasures in residential areas and the last block of Haight Street between Shrader and Stanyan — a block not yet fully covered by the adopted survey.

Both the adopted survey findings and the Counterculture Context Statement are publicly available for download at sfplanning.org. Residents who believe a building or site in the neighborhood merits historic recognition can contact HANC or SF Planning directly.

topStories.headline: Muni Adds Fare Inspectors Amid $307 Million Budget Crisis — N-Judah and Key Routes at Risk Without New Funding
topStories.dek: As SFMTA ramps up fare enforcement to close a structural deficit, Cole Valley and Haight riders face uncertainty about the long-term health of the N-Judah and other neighborhood lines.
topStories.body:
San Francisco's Municipal Transportation Agency is intensifying fare enforcement on Muni buses and trains, with riders caught skipping the fare now facing a $134 fine. The enforcement push, reported by Hoodline on August 16, comes as the SFMTA confronts a structural deficit of $307 million for the 2026–27 fiscal year — the largest budget shortfall in Muni's history.

The SFMTA Board of Directors unanimously approved a balanced two-year operating budget in April 2026, closing the first-year gap with a combination of a $200 million state loan, increased parking-citation late penalties, and higher parking-meter rates. The budget also depends on the passage of two November ballot measures: a regional sales tax through the Connect Bay Area Transit Initiative and a local parcel tax called the Stronger Muni for All measure. Together, those measures are projected to generate roughly $321 million annually for the agency.

For residents of Cole Valley and Haight-Ashbury, the stakes are particularly high. The N-Judah Metro line — the primary rail link for Cole Valley commuters — is listed among the routes that would face longer waits and reduced frequency if both ballot measures fail. The Haight Ashbury Neighborhood Council has flagged the regional transit measure on its website, noting that a 1% regional sales tax could allocate additional millions to help Muni stabilize.

Voters will decide the fate of both measures on November 3, 2026. The SFMTA encourages riders to learn more about the budget and provide feedback at sfmta.com.

events.title: Forever Grateful Exhibition – Haight Street Art Center
events.location: Haight Street Art Center, 215 Haight St (Lower Haight) & Golden Gate Park County Fair Ground Building (opening Sept. 5)
events.description: HSAC's Grateful Dead tribute exhibition includes the first-ever public showing of the original 1939 Furthur bus — the psychedelic school bus driven by Ken Kesey and the Merry Pranksters in 1964. A second chapter of the exhibition opens September 5 at the County Fair Ground Building in Golden Gate Park.

events.title: Counterculture Museum — Ongoing Exhibitions
events.description: The museum — named one of TIME's World's Greatest Places in 2026 — presents artifacts, posters, books, and memorabilia from the 1960s counterculture, civil rights, women's liberation, and LGBTQ+ movements. Open Wednesday through Sunday; admission $10.

events.title: Haight Ashbury Street Fair
events.location: Haight Street, Stanyan to Masonic, Haight-Ashbury
events.description: The 47th annual free street fair returns with three live-music stages, more than 200 vendors spanning food, art, clothing, and nonprofits, and a family activity zone. Attendance typically reaches 75,000.

moreNews.headline: Double Black Café Opens Inside Yardsale Flagship at 925 Cole Street
moreNews.body: Cole Valley's newest gathering spot, Double Black, officially launched in July 2026 inside the 3,450-square-foot Yardsale outdoor-apparel flagship at 925 Cole Street, taking over the former Pharmaca space. The café, co-founded by Cristina Ashbaugh and Kelly McGee — both Cole Valley residents and 2024 Shark Tank participants — serves espresso drinks using beans from Linea Caffe and drip coffee from Bird & Bear, a local Cole Valley garage roastery. Regular hours are 7 a.m. to 5 p.m. for coffee and 7 p.m. for the retail store.

moreNews.headline: Magnolia Brewing Back at Haight & Masonic Under New Local Ownership
moreNews.body: Magnolia Brewing reopened at 1398 Haight Street in December 2024 under new owners Kevin Kynoch and Brandon Phillips, following a brief closure during the ownership transition. The brewpub — one of San Francisco's oldest craft-beer establishments, originally founded in 1997 — has returned with an updated interior, a cocktail-forward bar program, and a menu focused on smaller bites, while gradually rebuilding its house-brewed beer selection. Updated Yelp reviews from August 2026 confirm the location remains open.

moreNews.headline: HANC Calls on Residents to Identify Historic Treasures in Residential Haight
moreNews.body: Following the SF Planning Commission's June 2026 adoption of historic survey findings for the Haight Street and Cole Valley commercial corridors, the Haight Ashbury Neighborhood Council (HANC) is asking neighbors to help identify historic resources in residential areas and the final block of Haight Street between Shrader and Stanyan — zones not yet fully covered by the formal survey. HANC meetings are held on the second Thursday of each month at 7 p.m. at the Park Branch Library, 1833 Page Street (except August).

restaurants.name: The Ice Cream Bar

hotels.name: Herb'n Inn

shops.description: The world's largest independent record store, occupying a former bowling alley on Haight Street and stocking hundreds of thousands of vinyl, CDs, DVDs, and music memorabilia across every genre.

shops.name: Cole Hardware
shops.description: Beloved independent hardware store anchoring Cole Valley's main commercial strip since 1920, carrying tools, housewares, garden supplies, and much more.

shops.name: Luke's Local

shops.name: Yardsale
shops.type: Outdoor gear and apparel brand flagship

shops.description: Colorful Haight Street boutique specializing in hand-dyed tie-dye clothing, hippie-inspired apparel, and accessories that celebrate the neighborhood's counterculture heritage.

shops.name: Decades of Fashion

shops.name: Relic Vintage

shops.name: Haight Street Art Center Shop
shops.description: The Lower Haight's nonprofit poster-art gallery sells limited-edition prints, screen-printed posters, and art supplies, and hosts printmaking classes open to the public.

shops.name: InoVino Wine Shop
shops.description: Cole Valley boutique wine shop with a tasting bar, focusing on small-production and natural wines available by the glass or bottle.

artEntertainment.name: Haight Street Art Center
artEntertainment.type: Nonprofit poster art gallery and printmaking studio
artEntertainment.description: Lower Haight nonprofit dedicated to poster and printmaking art, offering free gallery exhibitions, printmaking classes, and community outreach programs Thursday–Sunday, noon–6 p.m.

artEntertainment.name: Counterculture Museum
artEntertainment.description: Opened May 2025 at the iconic corner of Haight and Ashbury, this 4,200-square-foot museum — named one of TIME's World's Greatest Places in 2026 — showcases artifacts and exhibits on the 1960s counterculture, civil rights, women's liberation, and LGBTQ+ movements.

artEntertainment.name: Amoeba Music (Live Shows)
artEntertainment.description: The legendary Haight-Ashbury record store regularly hosts free live performances and in-store events, particularly around street fairs and album release dates.

artEntertainment.name: Kezar Stadium
artEntertainment.description: Historic 10,000-seat open-air stadium in the southeast corner of Golden Gate Park, hosting high school football, soccer, track meets, and community events since 1925.

artEntertainment.name: Kezar Pavilion
artEntertainment.description: Indoor multi-use arena adjacent to Kezar Stadium in the southeast corner of Golden Gate Park, used for concerts, community events, and sports.

artEntertainment.name: Panhandle Park
artEntertainment.type: Linear park and outdoor event space
artEntertainment.description: The eight-block-long eastern extension of Golden Gate Park, running from Stanyan to Baker along Oak and Fell Streets, hosting regular DJ sets, community events, and the neighborhood's beloved Hippie Hill.
artEntertainment.address: Masonic Ave & Oak St, San Francisco, CA 94117

artEntertainment.name: Buena Vista Park
artEntertainment.description: San Francisco's oldest park, offering forested trails and panoramic city views from a hilltop between Haight-Ashbury and the Upper Market neighborhoods.
artEntertainment.address: Haight St & Buena Vista Ave W, San Francisco, CA 94117

gymsRecreation.name: Folk Yoga – NoPa / Divisadero

gymsRecreation.description: LGBTQ+-owned boutique fitness studio in the Lower Haight offering small-group classes (max 6 people) and one-on-one personal training on a reservation-only basis.

gymsRecreation.name: Kezar Stadium Track
gymsRecreation.description: Free-to-use eight-lane all-weather track oval with a field events area, open to the public daily during park hours at the edge of Cole Valley and Golden Gate Park.

gymsRecreation.name: Golden Gate Park Panhandle

gymsRecreation.description: The Panhandle's shaded eight-block green strip is a hub for walking, cycling, dog walking, picnics, and informal fitness, and serves as a key bike-commuter corridor to downtown.

gymsRecreation.name: Haum Studios
gymsRecreation.description: Intimate Haight area yoga studio offering a variety of yoga and meditation classes in a welcoming community environment.

gymsRecreation.description: San Francisco's oldest park features a network of forested trails through eucalyptus and pine, popular for trail running, dog walks, and meditative hikes with city views.
gymsRecreation.address: Haight St & Buena Vista Ave W, San Francisco, CA 94117

gymsRecreation.name: CorePower Yoga – NoPa
gymsRecreation.description: Heated yoga studio in the NoPa/Lower Haight area offering CorePower signature sculpt, heated flow, and C2 classes with locker rooms and showers.
